findings.claim: The new 640/768px See all test is titled '…and the field stays readable', but at 768px it checks only that the field ends before the sort. Nothing bounds the field's width between 768 and 1023px, the band where the field still shares one row with a whole-value sort that cannot shrink.
findings.impact: From 768px the listing wrapper is a row (md:flex-row). The sort now sits in a `shrink-0` box, and the NameFilter box is `min-w-0` with a default flex-shrink of 1, so the field is the only part that can give way. Commit 4be7884 reports that this exact squeeze hid the field's text at 640–767px. If the header's auto column is narrower than 260px plus the sort at 768–1023px (wider CI fonts, a longer ja sort label, a wider Target name), the field shrinks until its text is hidden, and no test fails. The 1024px case asserts 260px; the 768px case does not.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/videoapp/VideoShelfPage.tsx:315,322 and ReadingShelfPage.tsx:274 (`md:flex-row`, sort wrapped in `shrink-0`). NameFilter.tsx open container: `flex … w-full min-w-0 … sm:w-[260px]`. PageHeader.tsx:117-121,164-167 put `actions` in an `auto` grid column beside `minmax(120px,1fr)` and `fit-content(40%)`. name-filter-desktop.spec.ts (the 640/768 block): `if (width < 768) { expect(Math.round(field.width)).toBe(260) … } else { expect(field.x + field.width).toBeLessThanOrEqual(sort.x) }`. The WIDTHS 1024/1280/1440 block asserts 260px.
findings.repro: Mutation: add `md:max-lg:w-[40px]` to the NameFilter open container, or otherwise let it collapse at 768–1023px. Every name-filter-desktop case still passes: 640 is stacked, 768 checks only the ordering, and 1024 and up are unaffected. app-header-desktop.spec.ts at 768 checks only sameRow(field, h1) and the sort's position.

bucket_proposal.reason: I12 (r3) asks only for 'from 768px before the sort on one row', with no width, so no declared invariant is broken. The test title promises readability, though, and the motivating defect can recur in the untested band.

findings.proposed_fix: At 768px, assert a floor on the field's width (for example ≥ 200px, or exactly 260px if that is the intent), or name the breakpoint where the field returns to 260px and measure it.

findings.claim: The r3 revision of SPEC-CORE-099 I13 adds a promise that a non-listing shelf page from 640px keeps the sort on the title row left of the Target. The only test at 640px (app-header-desktop.spec.ts) now measures the stacked listing-mode layout, so neither the r2-reported non-listing right-end clause below 640px nor the new non-listing 640–767px clause is measured.
findings.impact: A later change to the non-listing `SortChoiceMenu` / `ReadingSortMenu` branch (a watch shelf without a profile, an unreadable Reading key, or a page still looking up its Target) could move the sort off the title row at 640–767px, or off the right end below 640px, with no test failing.
findings.evidence: invariants.md:9 has the clauses 'on any other shelf page below 640px … right end' and '… on any other shelf page from 640px, the sort menu is on the title row left of the Target'. app-header-desktop.spec.ts (the SHELF_PAGES loop, widths 640/768/1280) requires `header input[type=search]`, so it only runs listing-mode pages. The fixture fixtures/appHeader.tsx:140-147 mounts by=folder only. The non-listing branch is VideoShelfPage.tsx:331-337.
findings.repro: Mutation: wrap the non-listing SortChoiceMenu at VideoShelfPage.tsx:332 in `<div className="w-full flex flex-col items-start">`. No e2e or unit test opens a non-listing shelf page at 375 or 640px, so nothing fails.

bucket_proposal.reason: This is a test gap that r2 F1 already reported. The r3 revision widens it to a new band. The code's non-listing branch is unchanged, so no invariant is broken today.

findings.proposed_fix: Add a fixture page for a non-listing shelf (for example video-shelf by=watch with no profile), and measure the sort at 375px (right end) and at 640px (title row, left of the Target).

specification_compliance: The commit under review (7f1f4b57) changes documents only. The product effect since r2 comes from 036593c (the sort wrapped in `shrink-0`) and 4be7884 (the listing wrapper's row switch moved from `sm:` to `md:`), both in VideoShelfPage.tsx:315-329 and ReadingShelfPage.tsx:274-288.

I12 (r3), checked against the code: below 640px the wrapper is flex-col w-full, so the field fills the row and the sort is below it at its start. From 640 to 767px it is flex-col with sm:w-auto, so the field is 260px (sm:w-[260px]) and the sort sits below it at its start. From 768px it is flex-row, with the field before the sort. This matches as written.

SPEC-CORE-099 I13 (r3): the listing-mode clauses are measured by app-header-desktop.spec.ts at 640 (stacked, sort.left == field.left, sort below the field), and at 768 and 1280 (sort on the title row), with sort.right <= target.left at all three. The non-listing clauses are not measured (F2).
No e2e-layout fixture or parity test mirrors the listing wrapper's class string; a grep for the class finds only the two shelf pages. The breakpoint change therefore needs no fixture update.
PageTabs, NameFilter, the Clips files and the store did not change since r2. Their earlier compliance readings stand.
potential_unspecified_behavior: From 768 to about 1023px, the name field may be narrower than 260px because it is the only shrinkable item beside a `shrink-0` sort. I12 (r3) states no width there (F1).
regression_risks: The field's readability at 768–1023px is unguarded (F1).
The non-listing shelf-page sort placement is unguarded at both <640px and 640–767px (F2).

The See all header layout now has three bands (<640, 640–767, ≥768) declared only in invariants.md. docs/specs/addon-app-header.md and the spec's §1 'Field width' still describe the two-band sm rule, so a reader who edits from those may undo the md switch.
test_coverage: 640px stacked listing layout: app-header-desktop.spec.ts (field on the title row, sort below at the field's left, before the Target) and name-filter-desktop.spec.ts (field 260px, sort below it, no overflow in the sort button, sort before the Target), in en and ja.
768px: sort and field on one row, the sort's value not clipped, the sort before the Target. The field's width is unchecked (F1).
1024/1280/1440px: field 260px before the sort on one row.
Non-listing shelf pages at any width: untested (F2).
not_verified: I ran no Playwright, vitest or typecheck run, so I did not confirm that the new 640 and 768px cases pass on CI fonts.
I did not compute the actual grid column widths at 768px in the real app shell (with any sidebar). F1's squeeze is inferred from the flex and grid rules, not measured.
I did not read decisions.md lines 3 and 15 in full (long lines), so I did not check the R-5 re-check record word for word.
I did not re-read the full bodies of the Clips files, LibraryFace, libraryFilters or PageTabs this round; they are unchanged since r2 and were read through the supplied diff.
trajectory: Each fix round has added a branch to the same layout invariant, so the See all header design is being patched. In r1→r2 (5c0a18297, documents only), SPEC-CORE-099 I13 was split into listing-mode and other shelf pages below 640px, matching the existing `listing ? … : …` code branch. In r2→r3, 036593c added a new layout constraint (the sort in a `shrink-0` box, so the field gives way). 4be7884 then added a new breakpoint state: the row switch moved from sm to md, which creates a 640–767px stacked band. The invariants were revised a second time, I12 (r3) and SPEC-CORE-099 I13 (r3), adding a third width band and a further listing/non-listing split at 640 vs 768px. No round removed a branch or state. Each new band moves the squeeze to the next width up, and the band from 768px, where the field can still shrink, is not bounded by a test (F1).
